claims.text: Mn promotes local chemical short-range order or atomic clustering in equiatomic Cr-Mn-Fe-Co-Ni.
Local SRO or atomic clustering raises local energy barriers for dislocation glide.
The quinary alloy has higher yield strength and strain hardening than the equiatomic quaternary and ternary FCC subsets.
The quaternary and ternary FCC subsets have more homogeneous atomic distributions than the quinary alloy.
The compared quinary, quaternary, and ternary alloys are all single-phase FCC after thermomechanical processing.
All alloy variants will receive identical thermomechanical processing and room-temperature deformation testing at a controlled strain rate such as 10^-4 s^-1.
APT and TEM can be used to assess local chemical ordering or atomic clustering.
Identical processing histories and controlled strain rates ensure that differences in mechanical response arise solely from composition and associated local ordering.
The alloy variants differ in the degree and spatial distribution of chemical SRO or atomic clustering.
The additional Mn in the quinary alloy enhances atomic clustering.
Mn-enhanced clustering increases the local Peierls barrier for dislocation glide.
More uniform atomic distributions in the lower-component subsets facilitate easier dislocation motion.
Easier dislocation motion in the lower-component subsets produces lower strength and work hardening.
Relative to the quinary baseline, the quaternary and ternary alloys will have lower SRO or clustering levels.
Relative to the quinary baseline, the quaternary and ternary alloys will have lower yield strengths and reduced strain hardening.
Local ordering will correlate positively with yield strength and strain-hardening enhancement.
The hypothesis is restricted to single-phase FCC alloys with identical processing histories tested at room temperature.
The hypothesis excludes comparisons affected by grain-size differences, other microstructural heterogeneities, or phase transformations.
Failure to observe significantly greater local ordering in the quinary alloy would falsify the hypothesis.
Failure to observe a correlation between ordering and enhanced yield strength or strain hardening would falsify the hypothesis.
